title: Capacity signal enrichment and automated healing for Dedicated pools
creator: Priya Raman
description: Summary: During the incident on 2026-03-03 we observed a dedicated customer fleet experiencing a capacity shortfall despite autoscaler health signals reporting within thresholds. Root cause analysis shows a regression in the backlog estimator combined with slow signal propagation for per-pool request-rate derivatives and KV-cache warmup. This ticket proposes a two-part mitigation: 1) enrich autoscaler signals (queue length, rate derivative, per-model concurrency, GPU utilization, KV-cache hit trajectory) and 2) an automated healing policy that performs controlled emergency actions (spawn burst nodes from reserved pool, temporary tenant shedding by priority, controlled fallback to quantized model variants) when composite risk crosses a calibrated threshold. The goal is to reduce mean time-to-recover from sustained shortfalls and avoid SLA breaches while minimizing noisy scaling and false positives.
notes: Acceptance criteria: (1) Autoscaler triggers automated heal in synthetic regression test within 90s of induced shortfall; (2) On real incidents, mean time-to-recover (MTTR) attributable to autoscale failures improves by >=50% vs baseline; (3) No measurable increase in false positive emergency heals in 72h stress window. Success metrics: P95 recovery time, number of emergency-scale actions per week, customer SLA breach count.
